title: A nonsplit small extension is an essential surjection
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative Noetherian ring and $k$ a field of finite type over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], [def-weil-field], [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Use the category $\mathcal C_{R,k}$ of Artinian local $R$-algebras with specified residue field $k$ and local maps inducing the identity on $k$ [def-sfb-artin-deformation-test-category]. Let $p:B\twoheadrightarrow A$ be a small extension. Either $p$ has a section in $\mathcal C_{R,k}$, or it is essential: whenever $D\in\mathcal C_{R,k}$ and $g:D\to B$ has $p\circ g$ surjective, $g$ is surjective. In the latter case the same conclusion holds if $D$ is any complete Noetherian local $R$-algebra with residue field $k$ and $g$ is a local $R$-map inducing the identity on $k$.

source.place: Tag 06H0 (lemma-essential-surjection), part (4); the complete-source version follows by factoring its map to the Artinian target through an Artinian quotient.

proof.text: Put $I=\ker(p)$. By [def-sfb-artin-deformation-test-category], $I$ is one-dimensional over $k$ and $\mathfrak m_BI=0$. Suppose $g:D\to B$ is a local $R$-map inducing the identity on $k$ and $pg$ is surjective; for now $D$ can be either of the sources allowed in the statement. Put $C=g(D)\subseteq B$, a subring containing the image of $R$. For each $b\in B$, surjectivity of $pg$ gives $c\in C$ with $p(c)=p(b)$, hence $b=c+i$ for $i\in I$. Moreover $C\to k$ is surjective: lift a residue class to $D$ and apply $g$.

source.place: Tag 06H0 (lemma-essential-surjection), proof of (4); explicit image/kernel argument replacing the length comparison

proof.text: Assume that $g$ is not surjective, so $C\ne B$. If $0\ne x\in C\cap I$, then every $y\in I$ has the form $\lambda x$ for some $\lambda\in k$, since $I$ is one-dimensional. Choose $c_\lambda\in C$ with residue $\lambda$. The scalar action on $I$ is multiplication by any lift in $B$, because $\mathfrak m_BI=0$; thus $y=c_\lambda x\in C$. This gives $I\subseteq C$, and the decomposition $b=c+i$ of step 1 would give $B=C$, a contradiction. Consequently $C\cap I=0$, so $p|_C:C\to A$ is injective as well as surjective.

source.place: Tag 06H0 (lemma-essential-surjection), proof of (4); explicit image/kernel argument replacing the length comparison

proof.text: For each $a\in A$ let $s(a)$ be the unique $c\in C$ with $p(c)=a$. Uniqueness shows $s(a+a')=s(a)+s(a')$, $s(aa')=s(a)s(a')$ and $s(1)=1$, by applying $p$ to both sides. Likewise, for $r\in R$, the image of $r$ in $B$ lies in $C$ and maps to its image in $A$, so $s$ is an $R$-map. Since $p$ induces the identity on $k$, the equality $ps=\mathrm{id}_A$ gives $\operatorname{res}_B(s(a))=\operatorname{res}_A(a)$. Hence $s$ is local and induces the identity on $k$; it is a section in $\mathcal C_{R,k}$, as defined in [def-sfb-artin-deformation-test-category].

source.place: Tag 06H0 (lemma-essential-surjection), proof of (4); explicit image/kernel argument replacing the length comparison

proof.text: If $p$ has no section, steps 1--3 rule out any nonsurjective $g$ with $pg$ surjective. Taking Artinian $D$ proves essentiality, and taking complete Noetherian local $D$ proves the last assertion. The argument used only the residue-field condition on $D$, so it does not require a separate factorization through an Artinian quotient. If a section $s$ exists, it cannot be surjective: otherwise $ps=\mathrm{id}_A$ and surjectivity of $s$ give $sp=\mathrm{id}_B$, contradicting the nonzero kernel of a small extension. Thus $g=s$ also shows that the section case is not essential.

The statement and every field except status/proof/proof_deps/proof_origin/mathlib_searches/split_report match live, where the item is still unsplit with no proof (no supersession). Four elementary steps cite only the definition. Step 1: B=C+I with C=g(D), and C->k is surjective because g induces the identity on k. Step 2: x in C∩I nonzero gives I=kx; the scalar action is multiplication by any lift because m_B I=0, and the lift can be taken in C, so I⊆C, B=C, contradiction; hence p|_C is bijective. Step 3: the inverse s is a ring and R-map, and res_B s=res_A p s=res_A gives locality and the identity on k, so s is a section in C_{R,k}. Step 4: without a section, essentiality holds for Artinian and complete Noetherian D alike; with a section, s is not surjective because the kernel is nonzero, so p is not essential (the converse of 06H0(4)). The direct argument correctly replaces the source's length comparison and the Artinian-quotient reduction named in source.place.
